MEFPP: Multi-Extension FITS Pre-Processing engine

MEFPP is a processing software for visual images of mosaic camera. It is a branch of the original wfi recipes prepared by Nick Devillard for the BeoWFI project using the eclipse package. The branch was created to support the WFI instrument at ESO’s La Silla Observatory while the author was the instrument scientist there. Then that branch was further modified to port those recipes to OmegaCAM once the author was transferred to Paranal to become the OmegaCam Instrument Scientist. One of the characteristic of this package is that it maintains the integrity of the Multi-Extension FITS files, MEF files, without splitting them into their extensions. Given the complexity of data management when reducing astronomical data it was felt that a factor of 8 in the number of files produced is too high a price to pay for reducing the complexity of the software by working with simple FITS files. For OmegaCam the factor is 32 making the data explosion in reduction even more extreme.

Although this package could be used stand-alone it is really intended to be use with the package PyCAVI, developed with Lientur Celedon. That package permits the efficient classification, association, and reduction of mosaic data, specially those data received as part of a service mode program or programs. These data has the bad characteristics that a single target observation can be split during multiple nights spanning months, semesters and even years. In this case the data management become the main road-block to efficient work. That package take care of all this, and provide a most needed data visualization interface that permits the checking of quality control variables. This is specially important when reducing WFI data which never had strong support from the ESO quality control group in Garching.

An example reduction session can be found in the Tutorial so that a user can get started quickly. The program can be used to create the needed calibration files and then reduce the data in one go, or to first produce the calibration data, and only then reduce the science data with the calibrations previously determined.

The mefpp pre-processing engine is written in C and based on the Eclipse and qfits software package. It modifies extensively the Eclipse wfi package. The current version is based in eclipse-5.0.0, qfits-5.4.0, amd mefpp-1.5.0. Everything is distributed together as a tar file.

Note that the best starting point is the guide for those in a hurry.

For detailed step-by-step guide see the tutorial .

An extensive description of the software cab be found at Description.
